{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "ULTRA MASTER PROMPT – Create a premium luxury art changelog landing page in Nuxt, fully static, inspired by the cinematic browsing experience of Netflix but for a high-end digital art archive. The website is called “Atelier Release Notes” and it should feel like a private collector’s room where every update to an artist’s body of work is presented like a new season drop. IMPORTANT: this is a STATIC front-end only website, no backend, no auth, no database, no real APIs, no CMS. Use mock/static/sample content directly in the project. Build it as a polished landing page / editorial showcase that can be exported as a static site. OVERALL STYLE: luxury, cinematic, dark, refined, museum-grade, black velvet background, champagne gold accents, ivory typography, deep burgundy highlights, subtle grain texture, soft spotlight gradients, elegant motion, premium art-house mood. Reference feeling: Netflix-style hero spotlight, horizontal rails, immersive cards, episode-like release tiles, but redesigned for luxury art and changelog storytelling, not entertainment streaming. TECH: Nuxt 3 preferred, Vue components, static data arrays, responsive CSS, no external services needed. Use placeholder artwork images or gradient/image blocks if assets are not available. The page must look complete even with mock content. MAIN GOAL: create a complex landing page that shows an infinite-scroll changelog timeline of art releases, exhibition updates, restoration notes, collector editions, archive additions, and curator commentary. The user should feel like they are browsing endless premium art updates. REQUIRED SECTIONS: 1) FULLSCREEN HERO – cinematic dark hero with a featured artwork update. Big headline: “Every Masterpiece Has a Version History.” Subheadline: “A luxury changelog for evolving collections, restorations, drops, and curatorial notes.” Include primary CTA “Enter the Archive” and secondary CTA “View Latest Release.” Add a Netflix-like large background artwork panel with dark overlay, metadata pills such as “June 2026,” “Restoration,” “Collector Edition,” “4 New Studies,” and a progress / release marker. Include subtle gold frame lines. 2) TOP NAVIGATION – fixed transparent-to-dark nav with logo “ATELIER / NOTES”, menu items Latest, Collections, Restorations, Editions, Curator Notes, Archive. Include small button “Browse Updates.” No login button. 3) FEATURED RELEASE STRIP – horizontal cinematic rail similar to premium streaming cards but for art changelog entries. Cards: “Nocturne Series v2.1,” “Gold Leaf Restoration,” “Studio Letters Added,” “Collector Print Drop,” “Sculpture Archive Expansion,” “Pigment Study Revision.” Each card needs date, category, short description, status badge like New / Revised / Archived / Limited. Static only. 4) INFINITE SCROLL CHANGELOG – the most important part. Make a long vertical feed that visually supports infinite scrolling. Since there is no backend, use a large static/mock list and optionally loop/render repeated batches on the client from local arrays only. No remote fetch. Each changelog item should be elegant and detailed: version number, date, artwork title, category, curator note, what changed, before/after mini panels, tags, edition badge, estimated reading time. The design should make it feel endless, with sticky year markers and alternating layouts. Add at least 24 sample entries covering 2023–2026. 5) NETFLIX-STYLE CATEGORY RAILS – several horizontal sections: “Recently Restored,” “New to the Private Archive,” “Limited Editions,” “Curator’s Picks,” “Studies & Sketches,” “Previously Unseen.” Each should have luxury cards with hover states, artwork placeholders, and changelog labels. 6) VERSION STORY SECTION – a dramatic editorial section explaining how an artwork evolves: Original Study → Restoration Scan → Curator Annotation → Collector Release. Use a 4-step luxury timeline with gold lines and large typography. 7) CURATOR NOTES – editorial cards with quotes from fictional curators, no real people needed. Example: “The June revision reveals a cooler underpainting beneath the original varnish.” Include portrait placeholders as abstract monograms, no external images required. 8) ARTWORK DETAIL PREVIEW – create a featured panel for one selected artwork, with title, version history, release log, materials, provenance notes, conservation state, and a large image area. It should look like clicking a Netflix title card opened a premium preview, but it can be static on the page. 9) STATS / METRICS – elegant counters: 148 Archive Updates, 36 Restorations, 22 Limited Editions, 410 Curator Notes, 12 Years Indexed. Static numbers only. 10) EMAIL / COLLECTOR CTA – newsletter-style section but static form only, no submission backend. Text: “Receive the next archive dispatch.” Input and button can be decorative; no real integration. 11) FOOTER – luxury footer with sitemap, archive categories, fictional contact text, copyright 2026 Atelier Release Notes. VISUAL REQUIREMENTS: dark luxury color palette (#050505, #11100E, #C9A45C gold, #F4E8D0 ivory, #5A1F2E burgundy), elegant serif headline font feel, clean sans body font, huge cinematic headings, soft gradients, subtle blur, card shadows, thin borders, gold dividers, refined spacing. INTERACTION REQUIREMENTS: infinite-scroll feel on the changelog page/feed, smooth hover effects on cards, horizontal scroll rails, sticky nav, scroll reveal animations if simple CSS/JS only, active-feeling progress marker, responsive mobile layout. Do NOT use WebGL, Three.js, canvas game, physics, backend, database, authentication, real API, payment, account system, or admin dashboard. CONTENT REQUIREMENTS: all content must be mock/sample/static. Use realistic art-world language: restoration notes, varnish removal, provenance update, pigment study, edition proof, archive scan, curator annotation, exhibition note, frame conservation, catalog correction, private viewing release. The website should feel like a premium product launch page and a living changelog at the same time. RESPONSIVE: desktop should feel cinematic and wide, tablet should keep rails usable, mobile should stack cards beautifully and keep the infinite feed readable. DELIVERABLE: Nuxt static website with clean component structure if possible: Hero, Navbar, ReleaseRail, ChangelogFeed, ChangelogCard, CategoryRails, CuratorNotes, VersionStory, DetailPreview, Footer. Include polished styling and enough static sample data to make the page feel complete and complex.",
 "judge": {
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8",
  "model_sha": "94125d2bd83076b21eed33119525e29eaf3894f4",
  "request_model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8:novita",
  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
